written.myAnswer: Carbohydrates are a major source of energy, store energy (for example, as starch in plants and glycogen in animals), and can provide structural materials such as cellulose in plant cell walls.
Monosaccharides and disaccharides are generally sweet, whereas polysaccharides are generally not sweet.
Monosaccharides: glucose and fructose. Disaccharides: sucrose and maltose.
Sucrose is made of glucose and fructose.
Starch is a storage polysaccharide in plants.
An amino acid is an organic molecule whose central carbon is bonded to an amino group, a carboxyl group, a hydrogen atom and a variable R group: H₂N–CH(R)–COOH.
Many lipids, including fats and oils, are formed from glycerol and fatty acids. A triglyceride has one glycerol molecule joined to three fatty acids.
mRNA carries genetic instructions from DNA to a ribosome; tRNA brings specific amino acids to the ribosome; rRNA forms part of the ribosome and helps protein synthesis.
DNA stores hereditary information and contains instructions used to make proteins.

Monosaccharides are single sugar units, such as glucose and fructose. Disaccharides consist of two monosaccharides joined together, such as sucrose and maltose. Polysaccharides are long chains of many monosaccharides, such as starch, glycogen and cellulose. Carbohydrates provide energy, store energy and have structural roles.
Proteins provide structural support, act as enzymes and some hormones, transport substances, enable movement, defend against pathogens and help blood clot.

Fatty acids are molecules with a carboxyl group attached to a hydrocarbon chain. Saturated fatty acids have no carbon–carbon double bonds; unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon–carbon double bonds.
Most fats and oils are triglycerides, each consisting of one glycerol molecule joined to three fatty acids. They are energy-rich molecules that store energy for long-term use.
DNA has two antiparallel nucleotide strands twisted into a double helix. Complementary base pairing is specific: adenine pairs with thymine, and cytosine pairs with guanine.
DNA is transcribed to form mRNA. At a ribosome, the mRNA is translated; tRNA brings amino acids, which are joined in the order specified by the mRNA to form a protein.

Water is a solvent and medium for biochemical reactions, helps transport substances, participates in some reactions and supports stable conditions in cells. These roles enable biomolecules to function.

Exact amounts depend on the recipe, cooking method and serving size, especially for the unspecified burger. Approximate composition by mass (carbohydrate/protein/fat/water) per 100 g is: roti, about 55/9/3/30 g (for 40 g, about 22/3.6/1.2/12 g); plain burger, highly variable; cucumber, about 3.6/0.7/0.1/95 g; whole egg, about 1/13/11/75 g; cooked rice, about 28/2.7/0.3/68 g; potato fries, about 41/3.5/15/39 g; carrot, about 9.6/0.9/0.2/88 g. Thus rice, roti and fries are relatively carbohydrate-rich; egg is protein- and fat-rich among the plain foods; fries are relatively high in fat; and cucumber and carrot are water-rich.
